query: Michigan cyclosporiasis outbreak 2026 hospitalizations latest count MDHHS, weekly updates for July and August 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the key trajectory the caller needs:

**Latest MDHHS data (July 24, 2026):** 8,176 confirmed cases, 160 hospitalizations — the outbreak now described as likely the largest cyclosporiasis outbreak in U.S. history.

**Hospitalization trajectory:** 36 (Jul 6) → 44 (Jul 9–13) → 102 (Jul 16) → 160 (Jul 23/24). The context figures are confirmed.

**Case trajectory:** ~708 (Jul 7) → 2,640 (Jul 13) → 4,312 (Jul 16) → 6,571 (Jul 21) → 7,171 (Jul 22) → 8,176 (Jul 24).

**Peaking vs. declining:** Daily growth has decelerated sharply. Early/mid-July had single-day jumps >1,000 cases; by July 21–24 daily increases dropped to ~200–512 (6–7%). MDHHS said July 22 the outbreak is "leveling off." This is consistent with the peak in *daily new infections* having passed, though cumulative totals keep rising due to reporting lag.

**Source identified:** Yes — iceberg lettuce from **Taylor Farms** (central Mexico), linked to certain **Taco Bell** restaurants. Recalled across 27 states (~July 18). Note: an FDA positive test was retracted as a false positive (Jul 19–20), and as of July 19 there were no confirmed positive product samples, but FDA continued to focus on Taylor Farms lettuce via traceback evidence.

One caveat: the MDHHS official dashboard page returned a 403 and couldn't be fetched directly, so all figures come from multiple news outlets citing the MDHHS dashboard on matching dates — these cross-validate consistently.

key_facts: As of July 24, 2026 (latest available), MDHHS reported 8,176 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases and 160 hospitalizations since the outbreak began June 22, 2026.
July 24 saw +512 new cases (6.7% daily increase), sharply down from early/mid-July surges exceeding 1,000 cases in a single day.
MDHHS said July 22 the outbreak is 'leveling off,' with daily new infections slowing significantly — indicating deceleration of the epidemic curve.
Contamination source identified: iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms (Taylor Fresh Foods) sourced from central Mexico, linked to certain Taco Bell restaurants.
Taylor Farms recalled iceberg lettuce shipped to 27 U.S. states around July 18, 2026, and suspended distribution of Central Mexico iceberg lettuce.
An FDA lab test initially positive on a Taylor Farms de Mexico sample was retracted as a false positive (July 19-20); as of July 19 FDA reported no confirmed positive product samples.

Officials describe this as likely the largest cyclosporiasis outbreak in U.S. history; Michigan has by far the most cases in a multistate outbreak (CDC ~1,645 across up to 34 states mid-July; FDA cited a 9-state cluster).
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. stated around July 21, 2026 that officials 'have the outbreak under control.'
